distinguishing_features: Applies a compliant elastomer (low-modulus, high-damping) liner to the pipeline interior to absorb impact stress, versus prior art's data-driven prediction, operating-envelope restriction, or chemical pulse dosing
Mitigates erosion mechanically by extending contact time to lower peak contact stress below the erosion threshold, rather than by monitoring, capping duty cycle, or altering surface chemistry
Physical hardware change (HDPU/Thiokol coating, 10-15 mm) targeting sliding bed-load impact on the pipe bottom
Shifts mechanism from resistance-to-cutting (hard-facing) to impact-stress absorption
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to mitigate erosion of the pipeline bottom caused by sliding-bed particle impacts without relying on high-hardness surface treatments that fail under high kinetic energy or thermal spalling.
parsed.viable_reason: Compliant elastomer liners are a known, commercially available erosion-mitigation approach with plausible impact-stress-spreading physics at the stated slurry scale, though the extreme 60x force-reduction claim is optimistic.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art uses a compliant low-modulus coating to absorb impact energy; shifting from hard-facing resistance to elastomeric stress absorption is a genuine mechanism departure not suggested by the prediction, envelope-cap, or chemical-dosing arts.
